text:
$BTC

Asi se shodneme, že predikování ceny $BTC je fajn na diskuzi v bufetu nad párkem v rohlíku, v realitě je potřeba si uvědomit:

- $BTC neví, že v tom máte většinu úspor
- neví, že jste se napákovali skrze úvěr či hypotéku
- je mu jedno, zda jako trader máte long/short = likvidaci, kde o vše přijdete
- je mu jedno, zda z vás pohyb na cenu xxx udělá chudáka či milionáře

Za mě si teď klidně můžete hádat, kde najde dno.

Můžu vám sám za sebe pouze říct z vlastní zkušenosti: ze začátku budete racionální, řeknete, že je pro vás dno např. 74k, ale až to cena podstřelí, začnou hrát emoce, vaše pýcha dostane na frak, s klesající cenou to budete posouvat až nakonec kapitulujete, nadefinujete si cenu, kde 100% bude dno … a při pohybu nahoru budete ti, co budou v prvních řadách vyřvávat, že je to manipulace a nezačal bull run (byť začal).

Tak jsme si to vyjasnili a teď jdeme na graf:

Popis:

Modrá čára - týdenní trend, pro určení dna musíme nejdříve prolomit downtrend

První časová osa - $BTC v midterm year ukončoval nejprudší pohyb cca v polovině června - a tadá v době konání BTC Prague, náhoda? 

Druhá časová osa - poslední dva midterm roky našel dno v posledním týdnu listopadového měsíce (okolo 27.11.)

Takže souhrn: tu trendovku max do pár měsíců prolomíme, na 100$ do konce roku fakt nejdeme.

Neptejte se mě, kde je dno, je to stejné na úrovni “jdeme na 200k a tam prodám”.

text:
PROOF OF MONEY IS AN AMAZING READ. 
AUTHOR- Terrence Michael.

My Bitcoin journey has not only cured me of chronic anxiety, but is now a window into a world that few understand and fewer can describe. As a business owner of four decades, I thought I understood money. I know now I did not. I was going through the motions of compliance with the system intrenched by banks. I knew no other.
 
In reading about Bitcoin and related materials to satisfy an all-consuming curiosity, I have met some of the sharpest minds, not in person but via the knowledge that they share. Many of whom I feel I know. Filtering garbage improves daily, with deleting incoherent bigots, poor in substance, and sensationalist click-bate grabbers. It is how I discovered “Proof of Work”
 
It is a pity I did not discover this work earlier with many questions answered sooner. The best writers convey a message in just a few words. Michael is one. He tells a story about complex ideas in ways that are easy to grasp. He is not out to wow with his intelligence or vocabulary, but the content and volume leave no doubt of his proficiency in both. This work is a refreshing departure from the acronyms and slang that Bitcoiners use to appear smart and authentic but frustrate the reader.
 
Michael delivers the narration of his own writing with the smoothness and skill characteristic of those who have dedicated their careers to the craft. Chapters are unambiguous and subject specific, each layered to provide information that builds for understanding those that follow.
 
I found the material so stimulating that it made me ponder the subject, often losing out on some of what followed. No problem, this is a book I will listen to in the future. 
 
A lot of work went into this work that, ironically, seems to have slipped beneath the commercial world's radar. I came upon it by chance. I recommend it to all interested in the world of finance, investing and a curiosity about how a better world in all facets could look. Or to glean and understanding of money, not taught in schools, universities, and inconvenient truths withheld from everyday people.   
 
@ProofOfMoney

Bitcoin was born without formal governance, by design.
That didn’t eliminate governance — it simply displaced it.

Between 2014 and 2016, the development of Bitcoin’s core relied on a very small group of people,
funded through institutions such as the MIT Media Lab,
partly supported by private donations.

This does not imply authorship or “control” of the protocol.
But it did help stabilize development at a critical moment.

The lesson is simple:
when governance is not explicit, it still emerges —
through capital, institutions, and human incentives.

The next stage won’t be built on legends.
It will be built on systems that can respond and take responsibility.

→ 日本も円ステーブル対応を検討せざるを得なくなる可能性。

🇬🇧 Today in London, DeFi Technologies was proud to be part of Digital Assets 2026: Beyond the Hype, hosted by Canaccord Genuity - Global Capital Markets.

Our President, @Forson, shared the stage with @freddienew, Co-Founder & Chief Policy Officer at @bitcoinpolicyuk, Katharine Wooller, Chief Strategist at @softcat, and Colin Paul, Cyber Liaison to the UK at the @rcmpgrcpolice, in a panel moderated by Jason Sleeth, Managing Director at @CG_Driven.

The discussion focused on the continued maturation of digital assets – from evolving regulation and institutional adoption to the growing role of ETPs, tokenization, and digital securities in global capital markets. 🌎

A recurring theme was the pace of change. @Forson emphasized that while regulation – particularly in the UK – can limit retail access, it is also a key enabler of institutional adoption, provided it can move at market speed. 📈 Regulatory agility, rather than rigidity, will be critical as digital assets continue to evolve.

🌟 During the discussion, @Forson also took the opportunity to introduce and formally launch the new DEFT Valour Investment Opportunity (#DVIO) Index, designed to provide clearer, rules-based exposure to digital assets. The index reflects a growing need among investors for structured, transparent frameworks that distinguish between different classes of digital assets and help identify investment-grade opportunities based on assets under management, growth, and risk characteristics. 📊

As the market matures, such indices play an important role in bridging digital assets with institutional investment standards.

text:
Most new blockchains promise speed.

But a better question is: what new things will they actually allow people to do?

Every real wave of adoption in crypto followed a shift in capability. Bitcoin gave us peer to peer value transfer without intermediaries. Ethereum introduced smart contracts and opened the door to programmable finance.

Over time, the focus moved toward optimization. Lower latency. Higher throughput. More efficiency. Those things matter, but they mostly improve what already exists instead of expanding what blockchains are capable of.

@ritualnet is approaching this from a different angle.

Instead of just scaling current use cases, Ritual is built to expand what users and developers can do onchain, with the goal of bringing in a new generation of applications.

The starting point sits at the intersection of crypto and AI.

Developers today can build highly adaptive, intelligent products. But as these systems become more influential, it becomes critical that they remain open, neutral, and resistant to control.

Ritual moves in that direction by allowing smart contracts to access native onchain AI secured by the same trust assumptions that blockchains rely on.

The idea goes further than AI alone.

Ritual is designed for heterogeneous compute, meaning different types of computation can operate within one environment. AI models, zero knowledge systems, trusted execution environments, and future technologies can all fit into the same architecture.

For builders, this significantly widens the design space.

What makes Ritual especially interesting is that it is not trying to be just another chain fighting for users. The goal looks more infrastructural.

A network that other blockchains can lean on when advanced computation is required.

High performance chains can use Ritual for prover networks. Rollup platforms can rely on it for complex execution. Entire marketplaces around verifiable data or programmable IP can emerge from this foundation.

Rather than competing for blockspace, Ritual expands what blockspace can represent.

The next wave of adoption likely will not come from doing the same things faster.

It will come from enabling things that were not realistically possible before.
